textbookText: ii) Function & Structure: Drone does not collect food or sting, mainly mates; worker collects food, has a stinger, and performs hive duties. b) Write the name of C. What is the reason for being C sterile in nature? Write any one reason. Ans:- The name of C is worker bee. Worker bees are sterile because they develop from fertilized eggs but are not fed royal jelly continuously, so they do not become reproductively active like the queen. c) Which of these honey bees secrete pheromone? Write any one function of pheromone. Ans:- Honey bee that secretes pheromone is B (Queen bee) Function of pheromone is to regulates the activities of other bees in the hive, such as maintaining social order and inhibiting workers from laying eggs. 11. Explain how the division of labour occurs in bees. Ans:- The honeybee colony shows a well-organized division of labour, where each caste (queen, drone, and worker) performs specialized duties to ensure the survival and success of the hive. i) Queen Bee o The queen’s main duty is reproduction. o She lays thousands of eggs to maintain the population of the hive. o She also secretes pheromones that regulate the activities of other bees. ii) Drone Bees o Drones are the male bees. o Their sole function is to mate with a virgin queen during the nuptial flight. o After mating, they die, and those who do not mate are usually driven out of the hive in winter. iii) Worker Bees o Workers are sterile female bees and perform different tasks according to their age (age polyethism). o Young workers (1–3 days): Clean hive cells and keep the colony hygienic. o 4–10 days: Feed larvae with royal jelly and honey (nurse bees). o 11–18 days: Produce and secrete wax, build comb, and ventilate the hive by fanning wings. o 18–21 days: Guard the entrance of the hive against intruders. o 22 days onwards: Forage outside to collect nectar, pollen, propolis, and water. This age- and caste-based division of labour ensures that every need of the colony—reproduction, defense, food collection, brood care, and hive maintenance—is met efficiently. It is one of the main reasons for the success and survival of honeybees as social insects. ***
